 تَارَةً يَكْرَهُونَهُ وَتَارَةً يُسَوِّغُونَ فِيهِ الِاجْتِهَادَ وَتَارَةً يُرَخِّصُونَ فِيهِ إذَا لَمْ يُتَّخَذْ سُنَّةً وَلَا يَقُولُ عَالِمٌ بِالسُّنَّةِ: إنَّ هَذِهِ سُنَّةٌ مَشْرُوعَةٌ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ. فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ إنَّمَا يُقَالُ فِيمَا شَرَعَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إذْ لَيْسَ لِغَيْرِهِ أَنْ يَسُنَّ وَلَا أَنْ يَشْرَعَ؛ وَمَا سَنَّهُ خُلَفَاؤُهُ الرَّاشِدُونَ فَإِنَّمَا سَنُّوهُ بِأَمْرِهِ فَهُوَ مِنْ سُنَنِهِ وَلَا يَكُونُ فِي الدِّينِ وَاجِبًا إلَّا مَا أَوْجَبَهُ وَلَا حَرَامًا إلَّا مَا حَرَّمَهُ وَلَا مُسْتَحَبًّا إلَّا مَا اسْتَحَبَّهُ وَلَا مَكْرُوهًا إلَّا مَا كَرِهَهُ وَلَا مُبَاحًا إلَّا مَا أَبَاحَهُ. وَهَكَذَا فِي الْإِبَاحَاتِ كَمَا اسْتَبَاحَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ أَكْلَ الْبَرْدِ وَهُوَ صَائِمٌ وَاسْتَبَاحَ حُذَيْفَةُ السَّحُورَ بَعْدَ ظُهُورِ الضَّوْءِ الْمُنْتَشِرِ حَتَّى قِيلَ هُوَ النَّهَارُ إلَّا أَنَّ الشَّمْسَ لَمْ تَطْلُعْ. وَغَيْرُهُمَا مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ لَمْ يَقُلْ بِذَلِكَ فَوَجَبَ الرَّدُّ إلَى الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْكَرَاهَةُ وَالتَّحْرِيمُ مِثْلُ كَرَاهَةِ عُمَرَ وَابْنِهِ لِلطِّيبِ قَبْلَ الطَّوَافِ بِالْبَيْتِ وَكَرَاهَةِ مَنْ كَرِهَ مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ فَسْخَ الْحَجِّ إلَى التَّمَتُّعِ أَوْ التَّمَتُّعَ مُطْلَقًا؛
translated_text:
something the other Companions did, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had not prescribed it for his community, it could not be called a recommended Sunnah. At most, one could say that this was a matter in which the Companions could legitimately exercise scholarly judgment, or that whoever practised it should not be censured, because it was open to scholarly judgment—not because it was a recommended Sunnah instituted by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for his community. Alternatively, concerning the observance of the Day of Arafat through supplication and remembrance, one could say that there is no harm in doing so occasionally in response to a particular circumstance, provided it is not made a regularly observed Sunnah.

This is how the leading scholars speak about this and similar matters: sometimes they disapprove of them, sometimes they allow scope for scholarly judgment, and sometimes they permit them provided they are not adopted as a Sunnah. No scholar versed in the Sunnah says that these are practices prescribed as Sunnah for Muslims. Such a statement can only be made about what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prescribed, since no one else has the authority to institute a Sunnah or prescribe religious practices. Whatever his rightly guided caliphs instituted, they instituted at his command, and it therefore forms part of his Sunnah. Nothing in religion is obligatory unless he made it obligatory, forbidden unless he forbade it, recommended unless he recommended it, disliked unless he deemed it disliked, or permissible unless he permitted it.

The same applies to judgments of permissibility. For example, Abū Talha considered it permissible to eat hail while fasting, and Hudhayfa considered it permissible to eat the pre-dawn meal after the spreading light had appeared, to the point that it was said, “It was daytime, except that the sun had not yet risen.” Other Companions did not hold these views, so the matter had to be referred back to the Quran and the Sunnah.

The same applies to disapproval and prohibition, such as Umar and his son’s disapproval of applying perfume before circumambulating the House, and the disapproval expressed by some Companions of converting Hajj into tamattuʿ (performing ʿumra followed by Hajj), or of tamattuʿ in general;

translated_text:
or the view of someone who fixed a particular minimum travel distance for shortening prayers and held that they could not be shortened below that distance; or who held that a traveller may not fast while travelling.

Other examples include Salmān’s statement that saliva is ritually impure; Ibn Umar’s statement that marriage to a woman from the People of the Book is impermissible; Muʿādh and Muʿāwiya’s allowing a Muslim to inherit from a disbeliever; Umar and Ibn Masʿūd’s refusal to allow someone in a state of janāba (major ritual impurity) to perform dry ablution; and the statement of Alī, Zayd and Ibn Umar that a woman whose marriage was contracted without a specified dowry is not entitled to a dowry if her husband dies. They also include Alī and Ibn Abbās’s statement that a pregnant widow must observe a waiting period ending at the later of the two prescribed terms; and Ibn Umar and others’ statement that, when someone in ihrām (pilgrimage consecration) dies, his ihrām ends and he is treated as someone not in ihrām.

Further examples include Ibn Umar and others’ statement that stipulating a condition in Hajj is impermissible; Ibn Abbās and others’ statement that a widow is not required to remain at home; and Umar and Ibn Masʿūd’s statement that an irrevocably divorced woman is entitled to accommodation and maintenance. These and similar matters over which the Companions disagreed must be referred back to Allah and the Messenger. There are many such examples. Nothing constitutes prescribed religious law for the community except what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prescribed.

Those scholars who said, “A Companion’s statement is authoritative proof,” meant this only when no other Companion disagreed with him and no text was known to contradict his statement. If the statement then became widely known and they did not object to it, this constituted assent to that statement. It may therefore be said, “This is consensus by assent,” provided it is known that they assented to it and that none of them objected, for they do not assent to falsehood. If, however, the statement did not become widely known, then, if it is known that no other Companion disagreed with him, it may be said, “It is authoritative proof.”

But if it is known that another Companion disagreed with him, his statement is not authoritative proof, by agreement. If it is not known whether another Companion agreed or disagreed with him, neither possibility can be asserted conclusively. Whenever the Sunnah indicates otherwise, authoritative proof lies in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, not in what contradicts it. There is no doubt about this among the scholars.

Accordingly, if it is established that Uthmān ibn Hanīf or someone else considered it a prescribed and recommended practice to seek a means of approach to Allah through the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, after his death, without the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying for that person or interceding on his behalf, we know that Umar and the leading Companions did not regard this as prescribed after his death as it had been during his lifetime. Rather, during his lifetime they sought a means of approach through him when praying for rain, but after he died they no longer did so.

Instead, Umar said in his authentic, well-known supplication, whose authenticity is unanimously acknowledged by the scholars, in the presence of the Emigrants and the Helpers during the well-known Year of Ashes—when the drought became so severe that Umar swore not to eat clarified butter until the people enjoyed plenty again—when he sought rain through al-Abbās:

“O Allah, whenever we suffered drought, we used to seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet, and You would grant us rain. Now we seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet’s uncle, so grant us rain.”

And they would be granted rain. All the Companions assented to this supplication, and none objected to it despite its being widely known. It is one of the clearest instances of consensus by assent. Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān made a similar supplication during his caliphate when he led the people in praying for rain.

Had their seeking a means of approach through the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, after his death been the same as doing so during his lifetime, they would have said:

“How can we seek a means of approach through the likes of al-Abbās, Yazīd ibn al-Aswad and others like them, and turn away from seeking a means of approach through the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who is the best of creation and the best means of approach

The hadith of the blind man supports Umar and the general body of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. For the Prophet only instructed the blind man to seek a means of approach to Allah through his intercession and supplication, not through his person. He told him to say in his supplication:

“Say: ‘O Allah, accept his intercession on my behalf.’”

Even supposing that a Companion instructed someone else to seek a means of approach through the Prophet’s person rather than his intercession, and instructed him to recite only part of the prescribed supplication, omitting the remainder that included seeking a means of approach through his intercession, Umar ibn al-Khattāb’s practice would still be the one consistent with the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would refute whoever differed with Umar, and the hadith that this Companion narrated from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would be evidence against him, not in his favour. And Allah knows best.

As for the third category of what is called “seeking a means of approach,” no one can transmit anything concerning it from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that scholars would accept as evidence—as has already been discussed at length. it. It is therefore a matter of dispute, as explained earlier. Their disagreement must be referred to Allah and His Messenger, and each party must present his evidence, as in other disputed matters. By the consensus of the Muslims, this is not a matter warranting punishment. Rather, anyone who punishes someone for it is transgressing, ignorant and unjust. For the person who holds this view has said what scholars have said, while the person who censures him has no transmitted evidence—from either the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or the Companions—that must be followed.

It has been established that swearing by anyone other than Allah is impermissible, whether by the prophets or anyone else, as has already been explained at length. The scholars have also agreed that no one may make a vow to anyone other than Allah, whether a prophet or anyone else, and that such a vow constitutes shirk and must not be fulfilled. Likewise, swearing by created beings does not constitute a binding oath, and no expiation is required for it. Even if someone swears by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his oath is not binding, as mentioned earlier, and no expiation is required of him according to the majority of scholars, including Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Hanīfah and Ahmad, according to one of the two positions reported from him. Indeed, swearing such an oath was forbidden. If a person may neither swear such an oath nor use it to adjure a created being, how can he use it to adjure the Creator, exalted be His majesty?

As for petitioning Allah by a created being without adjuring Him by that being, this too is something that more than one scholar has forbidden. The authentic Sunnah of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his rightly guided caliphs supports this prohibition. For a person does this only on the understanding that it is an act of drawing near to Allah and of obedience to Him, and that it is a means by which supplication is answered. Anything of this kind must be either obligatory or recommended.

It is well known that petitioning Allah by created things is not prescribed, just as swearing by them is not prescribed; rather, it is forbidden. Thus, just as no one may swear by a created being, no one may adjure Allah by a created being or petition Him by a created being itself. Rather, one should petition Him only through means relevant to the answering of supplication, as explained in detail earlier. Reports and statements permitting this have, however, been transmitted from some scholars. “Those who say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’”

Ibn Mas‘ūd used to say in the hours before dawn: “O Allah, You called me, and I answered; You commanded me, and I obeyed. This is the hour before dawn, so forgive me.”

The fundamental principle governing this matter may be stated as follows: adjuring Allah by any created thing, or petitioning Him by it, must fall into one of these categories: commanded as obligatory or recommended; prohibited as unlawful or disliked; or permissible, being neither commanded nor prohibited.

If it is said that this is commanded or permissible, then either a distinction must be drawn between one created thing and another, or it must be said that this practice is prescribed with revered created things, or with some of them.

Whoever says that this is commanded or permissible with all created things must consequently allow Allah Most High to be petitioned by the devils among humans and jinn. No Muslim would say this.

If, instead, someone says that He may be petitioned by revered created things, such as those by which He swears in His Book, it follows that He may be petitioned by the night as it envelops, the day as it shines forth, the male and the female, the sun and its brightness, the moon as it follows it, the day as it reveals it, the night as it conceals it, the sky and He who built it, the earth and He who spread it, and the soul and He who proportioned it. It also follows that Allah Most High may be petitioned and adjured by the retreating stars that run their courses and disappear, the night as it recedes, and the dawn as it breathes; that He may be petitioned by those that scatter far and wide, those that bear heavy loads, those that sail with ease, and those that apportion commands; and that He may be petitioned by the Mount, a Book inscribed on unrolled parchment, the much-frequented House, and the raised canopy

and the brimming sea; and that He may be petitioned and adjured by those lined up in rows and by everything else by which Allah swears in His Book.

Allah swears by those created things by which He swears because they are His signs and His creation. They bear witness to His Lordship, His right to be worshipped, His oneness, His knowledge, His power, His will, His mercy, His wisdom, His greatness, and His might. He, glorified be He, swears by them because His swearing by them magnifies Him. We, however, are created beings, and we may not swear by them, as established by the scriptural texts and scholarly consensus. Indeed, more than one scholar has reported consensus that nothing created may be sworn by, and they have reported the Companions’ consensus on this. Rather, doing so is a forbidden form of associating partners with Allah.

Whoever petitions Allah by these things must, by the same reasoning, petition Him by every male and female, and by every soul to which He has inspired its wickedness and its righteousness. He must petition Him by the winds, the clouds, the stars, the sun, the moon, the night, the day, the fig, the olive, and Mount Sinai. He must petition Him by the secure city, Mecca, and consequently by the House, al-Safā, al-Marwah, Arafah, Muzdalifah, Minā, and other created things. It would also follow that he must petition Him by created beings that have been worshipped besides Allah, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, the angels, the Messiah, Uzayr, and other things, whether they have been worshipped besides Allah or not.

It is well known that petitioning Allah by these created things, or adjuring Him by them, is among the gravest reprehensible innovations in the religion of Islam, and its offensiveness is apparent to the learned and the general public alike.  بَلْ أَنَا أَسْأَلُهُ أَوْ أُقْسِمُ عَلَيْهِ بِمُعَظِّمِ دُونِ مُعَظِّمٍ مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ إمَّا الْأَنْبِيَاءُ دُونَ غَيْرِهِمْ أَوْ نَبِيٌّ دُونَ غَيْرِهِ كَمَا جَوَّزَ بَعْضُهُمْ الْحَلِفَ بِذَلِكَ أَوْ بِالْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ دُونَ غَيْرِهِمْ.
 قِيلَ لَهُ:
 بَعْضُ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ وَإِنْ كَانَ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ بَعْضٍ فَكُلُّهَا مُشْتَرِكَةٌ فِي أَنَّهُ لَا يُجْعَلُ شَيْءٌ مِنْهَا نِدًّا لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى فَلَا يُعْبَدُ وَلَا يُتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَا يُخْشَى وَلَا يُتَّقَى وَلَا يُصَامُ لَهُ وَلَا يُسْجَدُ لَهُ وَلَا يُرْغَبُ إلَيْهِ وَلَا يُقْسَمُ بِمَخْلُوقِ كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ 
{مَنْ كَانَ حَالِفًا فَلْيَحْلِفْ بِاَللَّهِ أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ}
 وَقَالَ 
{لَا تَحْلِفُوا إلَّا بِاَللَّهِ}
 وَفِي السُّنَنِ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ 
{مَنْ حَلَفَ بِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ أَشْرَكَ}
 .
فَقَدْ ثَبَتَ بِالنُّصُوصِ الصَّحِيحَةِ الصَّرِيحَةِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَجُوزُ الْحَلِفُ بِشَيْءِ مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ لَا فَرْقَ فِي ذَلِكَ بَيْنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ وَغَيْرِهِمْ وَلَا فَرْقَ بَيْنَ نَبِيٍّ وَنَبِيٍّ. وَهَذَا كَمَا قَدْ سَوَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بَيْنَ جَمِيعِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ فِي ذَمِّ الشِّرْكِ بِهَا وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مُعَظَّمَةً.
 قَالَ تَعَالَى:
 {مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ
translated_text:
protective amulets and hayākil (charms) written by the turuqiyya and practitioners of incantations. Indeed, it may further be argued: if petitioning Allah and adjuring Him by these things is permissible, then doing so with created beings is all the more permissible. The incantations and adjurations used to adjure the jinn would then be sanctioned in the religion of Islam. This position entails disbelief and departure from the religion of Islam—indeed, from the religion of all the prophets.

If someone says, “Rather, I petition Him or adjure Him by certain revered created beings, but not others: by the prophets alone, or by one prophet rather than another—as some have permitted swearing by such a prophet—or by the prophets and the righteous, but not others,” the reply is:

Although some created beings are superior to others, they all share this: none may be made a rival to Allah Most High. None may be worshipped, relied upon, feared, or held in awe; none may be fasted for, prostrated to, or turned to in hope. Nor may an oath be sworn by any created being, as established in an authentic report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever wishes to swear an oath, let him swear by Allah or remain silent.”

He also said:

“Do not swear except by Allah.”

And in the Sunan collections, he is reported to have said:

“Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated partners with Him.”

Authentic, explicit texts from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus establish that it is impermissible to swear by any created being. In this respect, there is no distinction between angels, prophets, the righteous, and others, nor between one prophet and another. Likewise, Allah Most High has treated all created beings alike in condemning the association of them as partners with Him, even when they are revered.

Allah Most High says:

“It is not for a human being to whom Allah gives the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood

then say to the people, ‘Be my worshippers rather than Allah’s.’ Rather, ‘Be godly scholars through your teaching of the Scripture and your study of it.’”

“Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted to Allah?”

Allah Most High also says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Him. They have no power to remove your affliction or transfer it elsewhere.’”

“Those whom they call upon themselves seek a means of drawing near to their Lord, striving to be closest to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is something to beware of.”

A group of the early generations said:

“Some people used to invoke the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels. So Allah Most High said: ‘Those whom you invoke are My servants. They hope for My mercy just as you hope for My mercy; they fear My punishment just as you fear My punishment; and they seek to draw near to Me just as you seek to draw near to Me.’”

Allah Most High has also said:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah, and is mindful of Him—it is they who will succeed.”

He thus made clear that obedience is due to Allah and the Messenger, for whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah. He also made clear that reverent fear and mindfulness are due to Allah alone. He did not command that any created being be held in such fear or treated with such mindfulness.

Allah Most High says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn in longing.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“So when you have finished, strive diligently.”

“And to your Lord alone turn in longing.”

He, glorified and exalted, thus made clear that these people should have been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and should have said, “Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn in longing.” Thus He mentioned

contentment with what Allah and His Messenger have given, because the Messenger is the intermediary between us and Allah in conveying His commands and prohibitions, what He makes lawful and unlawful, and His promises and warnings. Thus, what is lawful is what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful; what is unlawful is what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden; and religion is what Allah and His Messenger have prescribed.

For this reason, Allah Most High says:

“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.”

No one may take any wealth except what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful. As for funds in which a person has a shared entitlement, such as fay’ revenues, war booty, and alms, he must be content with what Allah and His Messenger have given him from them—that is, his rightful share—and not seek anything beyond it.

Then Allah Most High says:

“And had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us.’”

He did not say, “and His Messenger,” for sufficiency means being enough, and Allah alone suffices His believing servants. As Allah Most High says:

“O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you.”

That is, He alone is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you. This is the correct interpretation, held by the majority of the early and later generations, as explained elsewhere.

The meaning is that Allah suffices the Messenger and those who follow him. Everyone who follows the Messenger, therefore, has Allah to suffice him, guide him, help him, and provide for him. Then Allah Most High says:

“Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger.”

He thus ascribed giving to Allah and His Messenger, but placed the mention of bounty between them, for bounty belongs to Allah alone, saying:

“Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger.”

Then Allah Most High says:

“To Allah alone we turn in longing.”

He thus directed longing to Allah alone, not to the Messenger or any other created being. It is therefore clear that Allah has placed all created beings on an equal footing with respect to these rulings. He has not accorded to any of

the created beings—whether a prophet or an angel—the right to be sworn by, relied upon, turned to in longing, feared, or regarded with reverent fear.

Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. They possess not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.’”

“Intercession is of no avail with Him except for those to whom He gives permission.”

Thus, He—glory be to Him—has warned those who invoke anything besides Allah, making clear that these beings possess nothing alongside Allah, have no share in His dominion, and that He has no assistant or helper among created beings.

He has thereby severed the hearts’ attachment to created beings in longing, fear, worship, and seeking help. He has left only intercession, which is real; but Allah Most High says:

“Intercession is of no avail with Him except for those to whom He gives permission.”

The authentic hadiths concerning intercession on the Day of Resurrection likewise indicate this:

“When people come to Adam and to the messengers of firm resolve—Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary—each directs them to the next, until they come to the Messiah. He says to them, ‘Go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven.’

“He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘They will then come to me, and I will go to my Lord. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration and praise my Lord with words of praise that He will inspire me to utter, which I cannot now express. Then I will be told, “O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.”’ He said: ‘He will then set a limit for me, and I will admit them to Paradise.’”

He then related the remainder of the account. Thus, the Messiah made clear that Muhammad is the intercessor whose intercession is accepted because he is a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven. And Muhammad, Allah’s servant and Messenger, explained—being the best of creation and the intercessor of highest standing

وَأَكْرَمُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى أَنَّهُ يَأْتِي فَيَسْجُدُ وَيَحْمَدُ لَا يَبْدَأُ بِالشَّفَاعَةِ حَتَّى يُؤْذَنَ لَهُ فَيُقَالَ لَهُ:
 ارْفَعْ رَأْسَك وَسَلْ تعطه وَاشْفَعْ تُشَفَّعْ وَذَكَرَ أَنَّ رَبَّهُ يَحُدُّ لَهُ حَدًّا فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ الْجَنَّةَ. وَهَذَا كُلُّهُ يُبَيِّنُ أَنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ هُوَ الَّذِي يُكْرِمُ الشَّفِيعَ بِالْإِذْنِ لَهُ فِي الشَّفَاعَةِ وَالشَّفِيعُ لَا يَشْفَعُ إلَّا فِيمَنْ يَأْذَنُ اللَّهُ لَهُ ثُمَّ يَحُدُّ لِلشَّفِيعِ حَدًّا فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ الْجَنَّةَ. فَالْأَمْرُ بِمَشِيئَتِهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ وَاخْتِيَارِهِ. وَأَوْجَهُ الشُّفَعَاءِ وَأَفْضَلُهُمْ هُوَ عِنْدَهُ الَّذِي فَضَّلَهُ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ وَاخْتَارَهُ وَاصْطَفَاهُ بِكَمَالِ عُبُودِيَّتِهِ وَطَاعَتِهِ وَإِنَابَتِهِ وَمُوَافَقَتِهِ لِرَبِّهِ فِيمَا يُحِبُّهُ وَيَرْضَاهُ. وَإِذَا كَانَ الْإِقْسَامُ بِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ وَالرَّغْبَةُ إلَيْهِ وَخَشْيَتُهُ وَتَقْوَاهُ وَنَحْوُ ذَلِكَ هِيَ مِنْ الْأَحْكَامِ الَّتِي اشْتَرَكَتْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتُ فِيهَا فَلَيْسَ لِمَخْلُوقِ أَنْ يُقْسِمَ بِهِ وَلَا يَتَّقِيَ وَلَا يَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَيْهِ؛ وَإِنْ كَانَ أَفْضَلَ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ وَلَا يَسْتَحِقُّ ذَلِكَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ فَضْلًا عَنْ غَيْرِهِمْ مِنْ الْمَشَايِخِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ.
 فَسُؤَالُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى بِالْمَخْلُوقَاتِ:
 إنْ كَانَ بِمَا أَقْسَمَ بِهِ وَعَظَّمَهُ مِنْ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ فَيَسُوغُ السُّؤَالُ بِذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ سَائِغًا لَمْ يَجُزْ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ بِشَيْءِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَالتَّفْرِيقُ فِي ذَلِكَ بَيْنَ مُعَظِّمٍ وَمُعَظِّمٍ؛ كَتَفْرِيقِ مَنْ فَرَّقَ فَزَعَمَ أَنَّهُ يَجُوزُ الْحَلِفُ بِبَعْضِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ دُونَ بَعْضٍ وَكَمَا أَنَّ هَذَا فَرْقٌ بَاطِلٌ فَكَذَلِكَ الْآخَرُ.
وَلَوْ فَرَّقَ مُفَرِّقٌ بَيْنَ مَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَبَيْنَ مَا لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ قِيلَ لَهُ فَيَجِبُ الْإِيمَانُ بِالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَيُؤْمِنُ بِكُلِّ مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ الرَّسُولُ مِثْلَ مُنَكَّر وَنَكِيرٍ وَالْحُورِ
translated_text:
and the most honored of them before Allah Most High—that he will come, prostrate himself, and praise Allah. He will not begin interceding until permission is granted to him and he is told:

“Raise your head. Ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.”

He also mentioned that his Lord will set a limit for him, and he will admit them to Paradise. All of this makes clear that the matter belongs entirely to Allah. He is the One who honors the intercessor by granting him permission to intercede, and the intercessor intercedes only for those for whom Allah permits him to do so. Then He sets a limit for the intercessor, and he admits them to Paradise. Thus, the matter rests upon His will, power, and choice. The intercessor of highest standing and greatest excellence before Him is the one whom He has favored above others, chosen, and selected for his perfect servitude, obedience, turning to Him, and agreement with his Lord concerning what He loves and approves.

If the rulings concerning swearing by anything other than Allah, directing one’s longing to it, reverently fearing it, guarding against its displeasure, and the like apply equally to all created beings, then no created being may be sworn by, regarded with such fear, or relied upon—even if it is the best of all created beings. None of the angels or prophets is entitled to this, let alone any of the shaykhs or righteous people.

As for asking Allah Most High by invoking created things: if this is on the grounds that He has sworn by them and honored them, then asking by invoking all such things would be permissible. If it is not permissible, then one may not ask by invoking any of them. Distinguishing in this matter between one person who venerates and another is like the distinction made by someone who claims that it is permissible to swear by some created things but not others. Just as the latter distinction is invalid, so too is the former.

If someone were to distinguish between that in which one must believe and that in which one need not believe, he would be told: One must believe in the angels and the prophets, and believe in everything the Messenger has conveyed, such as Munkar and Nakīr and the maidens

وَأَمَّا قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{وَكَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا}
 فَكَانَتْ الْيَهُودُ تَقُولُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ: سَوْفَ يُبْعَثُ هَذَا النَّبِيُّ وَنُقَاتِلُكُمْ مَعَهُ فَنَقْتُلُكُمْ؛ لَمْ يَكُونُوا يُقْسِمُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ بِذَاتِهِ وَلَا يَسْأَلُونَ بِهِ؛
 أَوْ يَقُولُونَ:
 اللَّهُمَّ ابْعَثْ هَذَا النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ لِنَتَّبِعَهُ وَنَقْتُلَ هَؤُلَاءِ مَعَهُ.

with beautiful, wide eyes, the youths, and other such things. Is it permissible to swear by these created beings because one must believe in them? Or is it likewise permissible to ask by invoking them?

It is therefore clear that, when asking by invoking a means, if what is invoked is not a means by which the supplication is answered, there is no distinction between invoking one created being and another, just as there is no distinction between swearing by one created being and another. All of this is impermissible. Thus, its impermissibility is clear, as those scholars who held this view have stated. And Allah knows best.

As for the words of Allah Most High:

“Previously, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved,”

the Jews used to say to the polytheists: “This Prophet will soon be sent, and we shall fight you alongside him and kill you.” They were not adjuring Allah by the Prophet himself, nor asking Him by invoking him. Or they would say:

“O Allah, send this unlettered Prophet so that we may follow him and kill these people alongside him.”

This is the established account among the scholars of Quranic exegesis, and it is what the Quran indicates, for Allah Most High said:

“Previously, they used to pray for victory.”

Praying for victory means seeking help to prevail: asking for triumph and victory. Seeking triumph and victory through him meant asking that he be sent, so that they could fight their enemies alongside him and thereby gain victory. It did not mean swearing by him or asking by invoking him. Had that been the case, they would have gained victory whenever they asked by invoking him or swore by him. Yet that was not what happened. Rather, when Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Allah granted those who believed in him and fought alongside him victory over those who opposed him.

What some commentators have mentioned—that they used to swear by him or ask by invoking him—is an anomalous report that contradicts the many widely transmitted accounts to the contrary. We have mentioned some of these in “Proofs of Prophethood” and in the book “Seeking Help

Abū al-Āliya and others said:

“When the Jews sought victory through Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, over the Arab polytheists, they would say: ‘O Allah, send this Prophet whom we find mentioned in our scriptures, so that we may overcome the polytheists and kill them.’

Muhammad ibn Ishāq narrated from Āsim ibn Umar ibn Qatāda al-Ansārī, from men of his people, who said:

“Among the things that led us to Islam—along with Allah’s mercy and guidance—was what we used to hear from Jewish men. We were polytheists and idol worshippers, whereas they were People of the Scripture, possessing knowledge that we did not have. Hostilities between us and them were constant.

“Whenever we inflicted something upon them that they disliked, they would tell us: ‘The time of a Prophet who is about to be sent has drawn near. With him, we shall slaughter you as Ād and Iram were slaughtered.’ We often heard this from them.

“When Allah sent Muhammad as a Messenger from Him, we responded to him when he called us to Allah, and recognized him as the one they had threatened us with. We hastened to him ahead of them and believed in him, whereas they disbelieved in him. These verses in al-Baqara were revealed concerning us and them:

‘And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming that which was with them—although previously they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved—but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.’”

 وَهَذَا الْحَدِيثُ رَوَاهُ الْحَاكِمُ فِي مُسْتَدْرَكِهِ وَقَالَ: أَدَّتْ الضَّرُورَةُ إلَّا إخْرَاجِهِ. وَهَذَا مِمَّا أَنْكَرَهُ عَلَيْهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ فَإِنَّ عَبْدَ الْمَلِكِ بْنَ هَارُونَ مِنْ أَضْعَفِ النَّاسِ وَهُوَ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ بِالرِّجَالِ مَتْرُوكٌ؛ بَلْ كَذَّابٌ. وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ مَا ذَكَرَهُ يَحْيَى بْنُ مَعِينٍ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنْ الْأَئِمَّةِ فِي حَقِّهِ.

 إنَّمَا نَزَلَتْ بِاتِّفَاقِ أَهْلِ التَّفْسِيرِ وَالسِّيَرِ فِي الْيَهُودِ الْمُجَاوِرِينَ لِلْمَدِينَةِ أَوَّلًا كَبَنِي قَيْنُقَاعَ وَقُرَيْظَةَ وَالنَّضِيرِ وَهُمْ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُحَالِفُونَ الْأَوْسَ وَالْخَزْرَجَ وَهُمْ الَّذِينَ عَاهَدَهُمْ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا قَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ ثُمَّ لَمَّا نَقَضُوا الْعَهْدَ حَارَبَهُمْ

‘But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.’”

As for the hadith narrated from Abd al-Malik ibn Hārūn ibn Antara, from his father, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbās, who said:

“The Jews of Khaybar used to fight with Sukayna, and whenever they met in battle, the Jews were defeated. They therefore sought refuge in this supplication: ‘O Allah, we ask You by the right of Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet whom You promised to bring forth for us at the end of time, to grant us victory over them.’ Whenever they offered this supplication, they defeated Ghatafān. But when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they disbelieved in him. Allah Most High then revealed:

‘Although previously they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved—but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it.’”

Al-Hākim narrated this hadith in his Mustadrak and said: “Necessity compelled me to include it.” This is among the things for which scholars criticized him, for Abd al-Malik ibn Hārūn is among the weakest narrators. Scholars of hadith narrators regard his reports as abandoned; indeed, they regard him as a liar. What Yahyā ibn Ma'īn and other leading scholars said about him has already been mentioned.

I say:

This hadith is among them, as is the other hadith he narrates from Abū Bakr, as mentioned earlier. Further evidence of this is that, by agreement of the scholars of Quranic exegesis and the Prophet’s biography, the words of Allah Most High:

“Although previously they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved”

were revealed specifically concerning the Jews who originally lived near Medina, such as Banū Qaynuqā', Qurayza, and al-Nadīr. They were the ones who formed alliances with al-Aws and al-Khazraj, and with whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concluded a treaty when he arrived in Medina. Then, when they broke the treaty, he fought them

—first fighting Banū Qaynuqā', then al-Nadīr—concerning whom Surah al-Hashr was revealed—and then Qurayza in the year of the Battle of the Trench. How, then, can it be said that this verse was revealed concerning the Jews of Khaybar, as al-Bayhaqī says? This account comes from an ignorant liar who did not even know how to lie properly. Further evidence of this is his mention that the Jews defeated Ghatafān when they offered this supplication. No one other than this liar has transmitted such an account. Had it actually happened, truthful narrators would have had ample reason to report it.

It should also be understood that, even if such wording implied petitioning Allah Most High by invoking him and adjuring Allah by him, a report of this kind could not be relied upon to establish religious rulings. First, it has not been established as authentic, and nothing in the verse indicates this meaning. Even if it were established, it would not necessarily constitute a prescribed practice for us. Allah Most High has related the prostration of Joseph’s brothers and parents, and He has related that those who prevailed over the People of the Cave said:

“We will surely build a mosque over them.”

Yet we have been forbidden to build mosques over graves. The wording of the verse states only that they used to seek victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it.

This is like the words of Allah Most High:

“If you seek victory, then victory has come to you.”

Istiftāh (seeking victory) means asking for triumph, that is, victory. An example is the transmitted hadith:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to seek victory through the poor among the Emigrants.”

That is, he sought victory through them—meaning through their supplications—as he said:

“Are you provided for and granted victory except through the weak among you, through their prayers, supplications, and sincerity?”

This seeking of victory may have consisted of their asking Allah Most High to grant them victory through the Prophet to be sent at the end of time, by hastening his mission to them so that they might prevail over their opponents through him—not of their adjuring Allah by him or petitioning Allah by invoking him. the disbelievers.”

Even if no transmitted reports had indicated that this is the meaning of the verse, no one would have been entitled to impose that disputed interpretation upon it without evidence, since the verse contains nothing to support it. How much less, then, when reports supporting this meaning have indeed been transmitted?

As for the previously mentioned account that the Jews used to be granted victory, we have explained that it is anomalous and is not among the well-known reports on this subject. The Jews are not known to have defeated the Arabs; rather, they were defeated by them. They used to form alliances with the Arabs, each group allying itself with another: Qurayza were allies of al-Aws, while al-Nadīr were allies of al-Khazraj.

The claim that the Jews used to prevail over the Arabs is therefore unsupported by any known account; indeed, the opposite is what is known. Allah Most High has told us what bears this out. He, Most High, said:

“Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except through a bond from Allah and a bond from people. They have incurred Allah’s wrath, and destitution has been imposed upon them. That is because they used to disbelieve in Allah’s signs and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.”

Thus, from the time humiliation was imposed upon the Jews wherever they were found, except through a bond from Allah and a bond from people, they did not prevail on their own over either the Arabs or anyone else. Before Islam, they fought only alongside their allies. Humiliation was imposed upon them from the time the Messiah, peace be upon him, was sent and they rejected him.

He, Most High, said:

“O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself, purify you from those who disbelieve, and place those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.”

And He, Most High, said:

“O you who believe, be supporters of Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, said

to the disciples, ‘Who will be my supporters for Allah?’ The disciples said, ‘We are Allah’s supporters.’ Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, while another group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became victorious.”

They had killed John, son of Zechariah, and other prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Allah Most High said:

“Humiliation and destitution were imposed upon them, and they incurred Allah’s wrath. That was because they used to disbelieve in Allah’s signs and kill the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and used to transgress.”

If, then, the Companions, such as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb and others, did not adjure Allah by the Prophet’s person, either during his lifetime—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—or after his death, but sought to draw near to Allah only through obedience to him or through his intercession, what, then, is to be said of invoking and petitioning created beings who are absent or dead—prophets, angels, and others?

Allah Most High has said:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim besides Him. They have no power to remove harm from you or to shift it elsewhere.’”

“Those whom they invoke themselves seek a means of drawing near to their Lord, seeking to be closest to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is something to beware of.”

A group of the early generations said:

Some people used to invoke angels and prophets, such as the Messiah, Ezra, and others. Allah forbade this and stated that those being invoked themselves hope for Allah’s mercy, fear His punishment, and seek to draw near to Him. They have no power to remove harm from those invoking them or to shift it away from them.

Allah Most High has also said:

“It is not for any human being to whom Allah has given the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to then say to people, ‘Be my worshippers instead of Allah’s.’ Rather, ‘Be devoted scholars of the Lord because you teach the Scripture and because you study it.’”

“Nor would he command you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have become Muslims?”

For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prohibited taking his grave as a place of prayer or a place of recurring gatherings. During his final illness, he said:

“Allah’s curse be upon the Jews and Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.”

He was warning against what they had done. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim both recorded this in their Sahīhs.

He also said:

“O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped. Allah’s wrath was severe against people who took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.”

Mālik related this in his Muwatta’. He also said:

“Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians exaggerated in praising Jesus, son of Mary. I am only a servant, so say: ‘Allah’s servant and Messenger.’”

Related by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

He also said:

“Do not say, ‘What Allah wills and Muhammad wills.’ Rather, say, ‘What Allah wills, then Muhammad wills.’”

A Bedouin said to him, “What Allah wills and you will.” He replied, “Have you made me a rival to Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills.”

Allah Most High said to him:

“Say, ‘I have no power to benefit or harm myself except as Allah wills. Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me.’”

Allah Most High also said:

“Say, ‘I have no power to benefit or harm myself.’”

And He said:

“You do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.”

And He said:

“You have no say in the matter.”

This is the true realization of monotheism, even though he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the most honoured of all creation before Allah and holds the highest rank with Him.

Al-Tabarānī related in his al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr that a hypocrite was harming the believers. Abū Bakr said, “Come, let us seek the help of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, against this hypocrite.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “Help is not to be sought from me; help is to be sought only from Allah.”

Near the end of Sahīh Muslim, it is related that he said five days before his death: “Indeed, those who lived

before you used to take graves as places of prayer. Beware: do not take graves as places of prayer, for I forbid you to do so.”

In Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere, it is also related that he said:

“Do not sit on graves or pray facing them.”

In the Sahīhs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, through Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayrah—with numerous chains of transmission through others as well—it is related that he said:

“No journey should be undertaken except to three mosques: this mosque of mine, the Sacred Mosque, and al-Aqsā Mosque.”

Mālik was asked about a man who had vowed to visit the grave of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Mālik said: “If he intended the grave, he should not go to it; but if he intended the mosque, he should go to it.” He then cited the hadith:

“No journey should be undertaken except to three mosques.”

Al-Qādī Ismāʿīl recorded this in his Mabsūt.

If someone were to swear an oath by the right of created beings, his oath would not be binding. There is no distinction in this regard between prophets, angels, and others. Allah, blessed and exalted, has a right in which no one shares—neither the prophets nor anyone else. The prophets have their rights, the believers have theirs, and they have rights over one another.

His right, blessed and exalted, is that they worship Him without associating anything with Him, as stated earlier in the hadith of Muʿādh. Worshipping Him includes devoting their religion sincerely to Him, relying upon Him, turning to Him in hope, and setting up no rival to Allah in their love, fear, supplication, or seeking help. Thus, in the Sahīhs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, it is related that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever dies while calling upon a rival besides Allah will enter the Fire.”

He was asked, “Which sin is the gravest?” He replied, “To set up a rival to Allah when He is the One who created you.”

Someone said to him, “What Allah wills and you will.” He replied, “Have you made me a rival to Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills.”

Allah, exalted is He, has said:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whomever He wills.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know.”

“And Allah has said, ‘Do not take two gods. He is but One God, so fear Me alone.’”

“So worship Me alone.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“So when you have finished, exert yourself.”

“And direct your longing to your Lord.”

And He, exalted is He, has said in the Opening of the Book, which is the Mother of the Quran:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“Among people are those who take rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“So do not fear people, but fear Me.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“Those who convey Allah’s messages, fear Him, and fear no one but Allah.”

Thus, when the polytheists sought to frighten Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him—Allah, exalted is He, said:

“His people disputed with him. He said, ‘Do you dispute with me concerning Allah when He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed?’”

“‘How could I fear what you associate with Him, when you do not fear having associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority to you? Which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?’”

“Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing—it is they who will have security, and they are rightly guided.”

In the Sahīhs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, Ibn Masʿūd said:

“When this verse was revealed—‘Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing’—it distressed the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They said, ‘Which of us has not wronged himself?’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told them, ‘That refers only to associating partners with Allah, as the righteous servant said: “My son, do not associate partners with Allah. Indeed, associating partners with Him is a tremendous wrong.”’”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah, and is mindful of Him—it is they who are the successful.”

Thus He made obedience due to Allah and the Messenger, for whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah. He reserved reverent fear and mindfulness for Allah alone: one should fear none but Allah and be mindful of none but Him.

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“So do not fear people, but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn with longing.’”

He, glorified is He, thus attributed giving to both Allah and the Messenger at the beginning and the end of this passage, as in His words, exalted is He:

“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.”

Yet He attributed bounty to Allah alone and directed longing to Allah alone. He, exalted is He, alone is sufficient for them; He has no partner in that.

Al-Bukhārī narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning the words, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best to entrust with our affairs”:

“Abraham said these words when he was cast into the fire, and Muhammad said them when ‘People said to them, “The people have gathered against you, so fear them.” But this increased them in faith, and they said, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best to entrust with our affairs.”’”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you.”

According to the majority of the early and later scholars, this means that Allah alone is sufficient for you and sufficient for those believers who follow you, as has been explained at length with supporting evidence. This is because the messengers, blessings and peace be upon them, are the intermediaries between us and Allah in conveying His commands and prohibitions, His promises and warnings. Thus, what is lawful is what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful; what is forbidden is what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden; and the religion is what Allah and His Messenger have prescribed.

We must therefore love Allah and His Messenger, obey Allah and His Messenger, and please Allah and His Messenger. He, exalted is He, has said:

“Allah and His Messenger are more worthy of being pleased, if they are believers.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

The first requirement is that you not set up another god alongside Allah: you must not love a created being as you love Allah, hope in that being as you hope in Allah, or fear that being as you fear Allah. a created being with the Creator in any of these respects has set up an equal to Allah and is among those who equate others with their Lord. He has taken another god alongside Allah, even if he also believes that Allah alone created the heavens and the earth.

The Arab polytheists acknowledged that Allah alone created the heavens and the earth, as He Most High says:

“If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘Allah.’”

Yet they were polytheists who took other gods alongside Allah. He Most High says:

“Do you truly testify that there are other gods alongside Allah? Say, ‘I do not testify to that.’”

He Most High also says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

They became polytheists because they loved those beings as they loved Him, not because they claimed that their gods created as He creates. As He Most High says:

“Or have they assigned partners to Allah who created as He creates, so that their creations seemed alike to them?”

This is a rhetorical question expressing denial, with the force of a negation: they did not assign partners to Allah who created as He creates, for they acknowledged that their gods did not create as He creates.

Rather, they took them as intercessors and intermediaries. He Most High says:

“They worship besides Allah what can neither harm nor benefit them, and they say, ‘These are our intercessors with Allah.’ Say, ‘Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on earth?’ Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.”

The man mentioned in Surah Yā Sīn said:

“Why should I not worship the One who created me, and to whom you will be returned?”

“Should I take other gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they rescue me.”

“Then I would indeed be clearly astray.”

“I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.”

And supplication is among the acts of worship. Whoever calls upon created beings who are dead or absent and seeks their aid—although neither Allah nor His Messenger has commanded this as obligatory or recommended—is introducing an innovation into religion, associating partners with the Lord of the worlds, and following a path other than that of the believers.

Whoever asks Allah Most High by created beings, or adjures Him by created beings, is introducing an innovation for which Allah has sent down no authority. If he condemns those who disagree with him and seeks to have them punished, he is unjust, ignorant, and transgressive. If he issues a judgment to that effect, he has judged by something other than what Allah has revealed, and his judgment must be overturned by the consensus of the Muslims. He is far more in need of being required to repent of this judgment and being punished for it than of having it enforced on his behalf and receiving assistance in doing so. All of this is agreed upon among the Muslims; there is no disagreement over it, whether among the four imams or others.

These matters have been discussed at length in several volumes, including a work in which we set out principles concerning judges’ rulings and the matters on which they may or may not pass judgment. It is a separate treatise dealing with the rulings pertaining to this subject. It would not be appropriate to include any of its chapters here, since the discussion in this place is devoted specifically to the principles of monotheism and related matters. An abridged portion of that work, with its chapters carefully refined, will be presented later in separate sheets for the thoughtful reader to consult, given the further benefit it offers and the pressing need to understand this important matter. Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah likewise agree upon what the Companions—may Allah be pleased with them all—agreed upon and what has been widely transmitted in the prophetic traditions: that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, will intercede for those of his community who have committed major sins, and will also intercede for creation at large.

The hadiths concerning intercession are numerous and transmitted through so many independent chains as to establish certainty. Several appear in the two Sahīh collections, and many more in the Sunan and Musnad collections.

As for the Waʿīdiyyah—those among the Khawārij and Muʿtazilah who hold that divine threats must be fulfilled—they claimed that intercession is exclusively for believers, serving only to raise their ranks. Some of them denied intercession altogether.

The scholars unanimously agree that the Companions used to seek his intercession and seek a means of approach to Allah through him during his lifetime, in his presence. Thus, Sahīh al-Bukhārī records from Anas ibn Mālik that whenever they suffered drought, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb would seek rain through al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, saying:

“O Allah, whenever we suffered drought, we used to seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet, and You would grant us rain. Now we seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet’s uncle, so grant us rain.”

They would then be granted rain.

Al-Bukhārī also records that Ibn ʿUmar said:

“I would sometimes recall the poet’s words while looking at the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he prayed for rain. He would not come down before every waterspout was gushing:

‘A fair-faced man, through whose countenance the clouds are entreated for rain,
A refuge for orphans, a protector of widows.’”

The seeking of a means of approach through the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb is explained in the other hadiths concerning prayers for rain. It is a form of seeking his intercession: asking him to supplicate and intercede, and asking Allah to accept his supplication and intercession. We put him forward to intercede and petition on our behalf—may my father and mother be sacrificed for him, and may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Likewise, when the people of Syria suffered drought, Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān sought rain through Yazīd ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashī, saying:

“O Allah, we seek intercession—and a means of approach—through the best among us. Yazīd, raise your hands.”

He raised his hands, and the people supplicated until they were granted rain.

 يَسْتَحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْتَسْقَى بِأَهْلِ الدِّينِ وَالصَّلَاحِ وَإِذَا كَانُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَهُوَ أَحْسَنُ. وَهَذَا الِاسْتِشْفَاعُ وَالتَّوَسُّلُ حَقِيقَتُهُ التَّوَسُّلُ بِدُعَائِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ يَدْعُو لِلْمُتَوَسِّلِ بِهِ الْمُسْتَشْفِعِ بِهِ وَالنَّاسُ يَدْعُونَ مَعَهُ كَمَا 
{أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَمَّا أَجْدَبُوا عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ أَعْرَابِيٌّ فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَلَكَتْ الْأَمْوَالُ وَانْقَطَعَتْ السُّبُلُ فَادْعُ اللَّهَ يُغِثْنَا.
 فَرَفَعَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ:
 اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا وَمَا فِي السَّمَاءِ قَزَعَةٌ؛ فَنَشَأَتْ سَحَابَةٌ مِنْ جِهَةِ الْبَحْرِ فَمُطِرُوا أُسْبُوعًا لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهِ الشَّمْسَ؛ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ الْأَعْرَابِيُّ - أَوْ غَيْرُهُ -
 فَقَالَ:
 يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ انْقَطَعَتْ السُّبُلُ وَتَهَدَّمَ الْبُنْيَانُ فَادْعُ اللَّهَ يَكْشِفْهَا عَنَّا. فَرَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ حَوَالَيْنَا وَلَا عَلَيْنَا اللَّهُمَّ عَلَى الْآكَامِ وَالظِّرَابِ وَمَنَابِتِ الشَّجَرِ وَبُطُونِ الْأَوْدِيَةِ فَانْجَابَتْ عَنْ الْمَدِينَةِ كَمَا يَنْجَابُ الثَّوْبُ}
 . وَالْحَدِيثُ مَشْهُورٌ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا. وَفِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ فِي سُنَنِ أَبِي دَاوُد وَغَيْرِهِ 
{أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ لَهُ: إنَّا نَسْتَشْفِعُ بِك عَلَى اللَّهِ وَنَسْتَشْفِعُ بِاَللَّهِ عَلَيْك. فَسَبَّحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَتَّى رُئِيَ ذَلِكَ فِي وُجُوهِ أَصْحَابِهِ وَقَالَ وَيْحَك أَتَدْرِي مَا اللَّهُ؟ إنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُسْتَشْفَعُ بِهِ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ شَأْنُ اللَّهِ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ}
 . وَهَذَا يُبَيِّنُ أَنَّ مَعْنَى الِاسْتِشْفَاعِ بِالشَّخْصِ - فِي كَلَامِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ - هُوَ اسْتِشْفَاعٌ بِدُعَائِهِ وَشَفَاعَتِهِ لَيْسَ هُوَ السُّؤَالُ بِذَاتِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ هَذَا
translated_text:
For this reason, the scholars said:

It is recommended to seek rain through people of religious devotion and righteousness; if they belong to the household of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that is better still.

The reality of seeking intercession and a means of approach in this way is to seek a means of approach through the person’s supplication. He would supplicate for those seeking a means of approach and intercession through him, and the people would supplicate along with him, as in the following account:

“When the Muslims suffered drought during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a Bedouin came to him and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have become impassable. Supplicate to Allah to grant us rain.’

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, ‘O Allah, grant us rain! O Allah, grant us rain! O Allah, grant us rain!’ There was not a wisp of cloud in the sky, but a cloud formed in the direction of the sea, and rain fell upon them for a week, during which they did not see the sun. Then the Bedouin—or someone else—came in and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, the roads have become impassable and the buildings have collapsed. Supplicate to Allah to lift this rain from us.’

“He raised his hands and said, ‘O Allah, around us, not upon us! O Allah, upon the hills and hillocks, the places where trees grow, and the valley beds!’ The clouds drew away from Medina as a garment is drawn aside.”

This hadith is well known in the two Sahīh collections and elsewhere. Another hadith, recorded in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and elsewhere, states:

“A man said to him, ‘We seek your intercession with Allah, and we seek Allah’s intercession with you.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, glorified Allah until the effect of this could be seen on his Companions’ faces, and said, ‘Woe to you! Do you know who Allah is? Allah is not sought as an intercessor with any of His creation. Allah’s majesty is far greater than that.’”

This makes clear that seeking a person’s intercession—in the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions—means seeking intercession through his supplication and intercession. It does not mean making a request by invoking his person. For if this were

translated_text:
a request made by invoking his person, then asking created beings by invoking Allah Most High would be more fitting than asking Allah by invoking created beings. But since it meant the former, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rejected the man’s statement:

“We seek Allah’s intercession with you.”

He did not reject his statement, “We seek your intercession with Allah,” because an intercessor asks the one with whom he intercedes to fulfil the petitioner’s need. Allah Most High does not ask any of His servants to fulfil the needs of His creation, although a poet spoke of seeking Allah Most High as an intercessor in words such as these:

“My intercessor with you is Allah; there is no Lord besides Him,
And there is no way to turn the intercessor away.”

These are objectionable words that no scholar has uttered. Likewise, some who hold that the Creator and creation are one have mentioned seeking Allah’s intercession—glory be to Him—with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Both are error and misguidance. Rather, He—glory be to Him—is the One who is asked and invoked, whom everyone in the heavens and on earth asks. He, blessed and exalted, commands His servants, and they obey Him. Whenever obedience to a created being is obligatory, it is obligatory only because it constitutes obedience to Allah Most High. The messengers convey Allah’s commands on His behalf: whoever obeys them has obeyed Allah, and whoever pledges allegiance to them has pledged allegiance to Allah.

Allah Most High says:

“We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah.”

And He Most High says:

“Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah.”

Those in authority, whether scholars or rulers, must be obeyed only when they command obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“A Muslim must listen and obey, in hardship and ease, whether willing or reluctant, unless he is commanded to disobey Allah. If he is commanded to disobey Allah, then he must neither listen nor obey.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator.”

As for an intercessor, he is a petitioner whose request for intercession need not be obeyed, however great his standing. An authentic hadith relates:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked Barīra to remain with her husband and not leave him after she had been freed and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had given her a choice, whereupon she chose to leave him. Her husband loved her and began to weep, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked her to remain with him. She said, ‘Are you commanding me?’ He replied, ‘No; I am only interceding.’”

She asked, “Are you commanding me?” and he replied, “I am only interceding,” because Muslims understood that obeying his commands was obligatory, whereas accepting his intercession was not. For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not blame her for declining his intercession. It follows all the more clearly that accepting the intercession of any other created being is not obligatory.

The Creator—exalted is His majesty—is far too exalted and majestic to intercede with a created being. Indeed, He—glory be to Him—is so exalted that no one may intercede with Him except by His permission. Allah Most High says:

“And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son.’ Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants.”

“They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.”

“He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.”

“And whoever of them should say, ‘Indeed, I am a god besides Him’—that one We would recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.”

The hadith cited earlier shows that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, may be asked to intercede with Allah, Mighty and Majestic—that is, he is asked to petition his Lord by way of intercession, in this world and the Hereafter. In the Hereafter, people will ask him to intercede so that Allah judges between them and so that they enter Paradise. He will intercede for those of his community who committed major sins. He will also intercede for some who deserve the Fire so that they do not enter it, and for some who have entered it so that they are brought out of it.

وَلَا نِزَاعَ بَيْنَ جَمَاهِيرِ الْأُمَّةِ أَنَّهُ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَشْفَعَ لِأَهْلِ الطَّاعَةِ الْمُسْتَحِقِّينَ لِلثَّوَابِ.
 وَلَكِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبِدَعِ وَالْخَوَارِجِ وَالْمُعْتَزِلَةِ أَنْكَرُوا شَفَاعَتَهُ لِأَهْلِ الْكَبَائِرِ فَقَالُوا:
 لَا يَشْفَعُ لِأَهْلِ الْكَبَائِرِ بِنَاءً عَلَى أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكَبَائِرِ عِنْدَهُمْ لَا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَلَا يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ النَّارِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوهَا لَا بِشَفَاعَةِ وَلَا غَيْرِهَا وَمَذْهَبُ الصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ وَأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَسَائِرِ أَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَشْفَعُ فِي أَهْلِ الْكَبَائِرِ وَأَنَّهُ لَا يُخَلَّدُ فِي النَّارِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ أَحَدٌ؛ بَلْ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ النَّارِ مَنْ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ إيمَانٍ أَوْ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ إيمَانٍ لَكِنَّ هَذَا الِاسْتِسْقَاءَ وَالِاسْتِشْفَاعَ وَالتَّوَسُّلَ بِهِ وَبِغَيْرِهِ كَانَ يَكُونُ فِي حَيَاتِهِ بِمَعْنَى أَنَّهُمْ يَطْلُبُونَ مِنْهُ الدُّعَاءَ فَيَدْعُو لَهُمْ فَكَانَ تَوَسُّلُهُمْ بِدُعَائِهِ وَالِاسْتِشْفَاعُ بِهِ طَلَبَ شَفَاعَتِهِ وَالشَّفَاعَةُ دُعَاءٌ.
فَأَمَّا التَّوَسُّلُ بِذَاتِهِ فِي حُضُورِهِ أَوْ مَغِيبِهِ أَوْ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ - مِثْلَ الْإِقْسَامِ بِذَاتِهِ أَوْ بِغَيْرِهِ مِنْ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ أَوْ السُّؤَالِ بِنَفْسِ ذَوَاتِهِمْ بِدُعَائِهِمْ - فَلَيْسَ هَذَا مَشْهُورًا عِنْدَ الصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ بَلْ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَمُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ وَمَنْ بِحَضْرَتِهِمَا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَالتَّابِعِينَ لَهُمْ بِإِحْسَانِ لَمَّا أَجْدَبُوا اسْتَسْقَوْا وَتَوَسَّلُوا وَاسْتَشْفَعُوا بِمَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا كَالْعَبَّاسِ وكيزيد بْنِ الْأَسْوَدِ وَلَمْ يَتَوَسَّلُوا وَلَمْ يَسْتَشْفِعُوا وَلَمْ يَسْتَسْقُوا فِي هَذِهِ الْحَالِ بِالنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَا عِنْدَ قَبْرِهِ وَلَا غَيْرِ قَبْرِهِ بَلْ عَدَلُوا إلَى الْبَدَلِ كَالْعَبَّاسِ
translated_text:
And there is no dispute among the great majority of the Muslim community that he may intercede for those whose obedience entitles them to reward.

However, many among the adherents of religious innovation, the Khawārij, and the Mu'tazila denied his intercession for those who commit major sins. They said, “He does not intercede for those who commit major sins,” because, according to them, Allah neither forgives such people nor brings them out of the Fire once they have entered it, whether through intercession or otherwise. The position of the Companions, the Successors, the leading Muslim scholars, and all other adherents of the Sunnah and the community is that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intercedes for those who commit major sins, and that no believer remains in the Fire forever. Rather, anyone whose heart contains a grain’s weight or an atom’s weight of faith will emerge from the Fire.

But this seeking of rain, requesting intercession, and seeking a means of approach to Allah through him or others took place during their lifetimes: people would ask them to supplicate, and they would supplicate for them. Thus, their means of approach was his supplication; seeking his intercession meant asking him to intercede, and intercession is supplication.

As for seeking a means of approach through his person, whether in his presence, in his absence, or after his death—such as adjuring Allah by his person or by another prophet, or petitioning by their very persons through their supplications—this was not a well-known practice among the Companions and the Successors. Rather, when drought struck, 'Umar ibn al-Khattāb, Mu'āwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, and those present with them from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed them in righteousness sought rain, sought a means of approach to Allah, and requested intercession through living people, such as al-'Abbās and Yazīd ibn al-Aswad. In these circumstances, they did not seek a means of approach, request intercession, or seek rain through the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, either at his grave or elsewhere. Instead, they turned to alternatives, such as al-'Abbās

and Yazīd. Rather, they would invoke blessings upon him in their supplications. 'Umar said:

“O Allah, we used to seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet, and You would grant us rain. Now we seek a means of approach to You through our Prophet’s uncle, so grant us rain.”

They therefore substituted this for their former practice when it was no longer possible to seek a means of approach through him in the prescribed manner they had previously followed. They could have gone to his grave and sought a means of approach through him, or invoked his standing in their supplications in the open country, using similar expressions that entail adjuring Allah, Almighty and Majestic, by a created being or petitioning Him by that being. They could have said, “We ask You, or adjure You, by Your Prophet, or by Your Prophet’s standing,” and similar expressions used by some people.

Some ignorant people have related that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When you ask Allah, ask Him by my standing, for my standing with Allah is great.”

This hadith is fabricated. It is not found in any of the Muslim books upon which hadith scholars rely, nor has any scholar of hadith mentioned it—even though his standing with Allah Most High is greater than that of all the other prophets and messengers. Allah, glorified is He, has told us that Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them both, held places of honor with Him. He Most High said:

“O you who believe, do not be like those who offended Moses. Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was held in honor by Allah.”

He Most High also said:

“When the angels said, ‘O Mary, Allah gives you glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, honored in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near to Him.’”

If Moses and Jesus held places of honor with Allah, Almighty and Majestic, then how much more so the leader of the children of Adam, the one granted the Praiseworthy Station for which the earliest and latest generations will regard him with admiring envy, and the one granted al-Kawthar

and the Pool to which people will come, whose vessels are as numerous as the stars in the sky, whose water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and from which whoever takes a single drink will never thirst again? He is the one who will intercede on the Day of Resurrection, when Adam and the messengers of firm resolve—Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all—step back from it, while he steps forward to undertake it. He is the bearer of the banner beneath which Adam and all others will stand. He is the leader of the children of Adam and the most honored of them before his Lord, Almighty and Majestic. He is the leader of the prophets when they assemble and their spokesman when they come as a delegation. His standing is immense; may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

Yet a created being’s standing before the Creator Most High is not like one created being’s standing before another, for no one intercedes with Him except by His permission:

“There is no one in the heavens and the earth who will not come to the Most Merciful as a servant.”

“He has certainly counted them and numbered them precisely.”

He Most High also said:

“The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near to Him. Whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant—He will gather them all to Himself.”

“As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and grant them more from His bounty. But as for those who disdain and are arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will find neither a protector nor a helper besides Allah.”

A created being intercedes with another created being without the latter’s permission, and is thus his partner in securing the desired outcome. Allah Most High, however, has no partner, as He, glorified is He, said:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. They do not possess even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.’”

“Intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits.”
